methodological_rigor.justification: The design fundamentally relies on a single pediatric cell line (SF188) balanced against five adult-origin lines; the authors explicitly acknowledge that 'pediatric' GBM is essentially represented by one biological sample. Although they claim no spectra from a given cell were shared between train and test, cell-level leakage is not clearly excluded (balanced selection of 364 spectra was random, not by cell). Preprocessing (StandardScaler, PCA on training only) and 10-fold CV are reasonable. The chosen architecture (5 hidden layers x 5 neurons) has CV accuracy of ~66% but held-out test accuracy of 83.6% — this inconsistency is not adequately explained. No independent biological replicate or external validation cohort exists.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical in vitro proof-of-concept using cultured GBM neurospheres on CaF2 substrates, not tissue or patient data. Clinical translation would require fresh tissue, in situ measurements, and multi-line pediatric representation (authors note this). Findings are hypothesis-generating for future Raman-guided intraoperative diagnostics. As preclinical/cell-line research, LoE maps to 5.

reporting_quality.justification: No applicable reporting standard is cited; ARRIVE is not relevant (no animals), and no TRIPOD-AI or DECIDE-AI checklist is referenced despite being a machine learning diagnostic study. Methods describe instrumentation, preprocessing, PCA, MLP hyperparameter search, and evaluation protocol in reasonable detail. No data or code availability statement is provided; spectra, trained model, and training scripts are not shared. Multiple typos (challanged, metabolsim, perfomring, 'DL metholody', 'ouf knowledge') suggest incomplete proofreading.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors claim this is the first application of Raman spectroscopy plus deep learning for pediatric vs. adult GBM classification at the stem cell level. Related Raman+ML GBM work already exists (refs 11, 22, 27-30 including Hollon 2018 intraoperative pediatric brain tumor Raman). Novelty is a methodological recombination rather than a fundamental advance, limited by the single pediatric cell line.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript communicates its main points but has numerous typos and awkward phrasings ('challanged', 'microenvirnmental paramters', 'metabolsim', 'DL metholody', 'perfomring', 'ouf knowledge', 'evidences' for singular 'evidence'). Figures and tables are described appropriately. Introduction and discussion have some circular/redundant passages and hedged conclusions that are nonetheless clearly stated.

key_strengths: Strict train/test split with preprocessing (StandardScaler, PCA) fit only on training data to prevent leakage
Spectroscopically plausible peak assignments tied to known biological differences in nucleic acid, lipid, and cytochrome content
Transparent acknowledgement of single-pediatric-line limitation and explicit framing as SF188 phenotype profiling rather than universal pediatric signature
Sensible simple MLP (5x5) chosen after hyperparameter search
key_concerns: Pediatric class represented by a single cell line (SF188); the classifier likely learns SF188 identity rather than a pediatric signature
Large gap between 10-fold CV accuracy (~66%) and held-out test accuracy (83.6%) is unexplained and raises overfitting/leakage concern
No patient tissue, no independent biological replicate, no external cohort — strictly in vitro proof-of-concept
No data or code availability statement; model and spectra not shared
No adherence to a recognized AI/diagnostic reporting standard (e.g., TRIPOD-AI, DECIDE-AI) despite being a prediction-model study
Numerous typographical and grammatical errors suggest insufficient proofreading
chief_reviewer.rationale: Interesting preliminary proof-of-concept undermined by the fundamental design flaw of one pediatric cell line and absence of tissue or external validation; suitable only for a lower-tier specialty journal after major revisions, including multi-line pediatric replication.
